Public APIs provide unrestricted access to public information for all exchange markets without the need to register a user account or have an API key.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePublic APIs include the following:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emarket data\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003einstruments/trading pairs\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eprice feeds (exchange rates)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eorder books\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003etrade history\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003etickers\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOHLC(V) for charting\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eother public endpoints\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIn order to trade with private APIs you need to obtain API keys from an exchange's website. It usually means signing up to the exchange and creating API keys for your account. Some exchanges require personal info or identification. Sometimes verification may be necessary as well. In this case you will need to register yourself, this library will not create accounts or API keys for you. Some exchanges expose API endpoints for registering an account, but most exchanges don't. You will have to sign up and create API keys on their websites.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrivate APIs allow the following:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emanage personal account info\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003equery account balances\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003etrade by making market and limit orders\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003edeposit and withdraw fiat and crypto funds\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003equery personal orders\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eget ledger history\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003etransfer funds between accounts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003euse merchant services\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis library all clients, and prevent abuse that could degrade performance or availability for other users. That means you can't make an unlimited amount of requests to the exchange, there is a rate that needs to be respected.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBy default, CCXT uses a \u003cstrong\u003eleaky bucket\u003c/strong\u003e rate limiter to control the pace of outgoing requests. A leaky bucket rate limiter works by queueing requests and releasing them at a steady, fixed rate. Bursts of requests are smoothed out over time rather than executed immediately.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHowever, if the user provides a \u003ccode\u003erateLimiterAlgorithm': 'rollingWindow'\u003c/code\u003e option, ccxt switches from the leaky bucket model to a \u003cstrong\u003ewindow-based rate\u003c/strong\u003e limiter. A window-based limiter enforces a maximum number of requests within a fixed time window (for example, N requests per X milliseconds). Once the limit is reached, further requests are delayed until the current window expires. By default CCXT assumes a 60s window but the window size can be customized by providing \u003ccode\u003erollingWindowSize: X0000\u003c/code\u003e ms.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eExample:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"exchange = ccxt.binance({\n    'rateLimiterAlgorithm': 'rollingWindow', # switching to rolling window algorithm\n    'rollingWindowSize': 5000 # if binance allows X requests per 5 seconds, those requests can be fired in a burst at any time during this window\n})\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eexchange\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e=\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-s1\"\u003eccxt\u003c/span\u003e.\u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003ebinance\u003c/span\u003e({\n    \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e'rateLimiterAlgorithm'\u003c/span\u003e: \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e'rollingWindow'\u003c/span\u003e, \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e# switching to rolling window algorithm\u003c/span\u003e\n    \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e'rollingWindowSize'\u003c/span\u003e: \u003cspan class=\"pl-c1\"\u003e5000\u003c/span\u003e \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e# if binance allows X requests per 5 seconds, those replace node-fetch with native fetch (undici), HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pooling (#29084)

* feat(base): replace node-fetch with native fetch (undici), HTTP/1.1 keep-alive pooling

* fix(base): rename fetch-prefixed internal helpers to avoid C# wrapper generation

* chore(deps): add undici 7.27.2 as an optional dependency

* reduce size of comment

* perf(base): dispatch node requests through undici.request instead of undici.fetch

* fix(base): cap fetchProxyDispatchers at 8 (FIFO), disable redirect following

Rotating-proxy setups grew the proxy dispatcher cache without bound:
every distinct proxy url cached a composed ProxyAgent forever, each
holding ~23KB of eagerly-allocated pool state (dominated by undici
PoolBase's preallocated 2048-slot FixedQueue), measured 45.6MB retained
after 2,000 rotations. The cache is now FIFO-capped at
fetchProxyDispatchersMaxSize (default 8, user-tunable); evicted
dispatchers are closed gracefully so their in-flight requests finish
first, and an evicted proxy url is transparently re-created on next use.

Redirect following is removed entirely (previously 10 via undici's
redirect interceptor): exchange rest apis do not redirect legitimately,
so following one can only mask a misconfigured endpoint or a tampered
response. The undici.request path drains the body (releasing the
keep-alive socket) and raises NetworkError naming the status and
location; the whatwg-fetch paths (browser / bun / global-fetch fallback)
set 'redirect': 'error', whose TypeError rejection is surfaced as
NetworkError by the existing handler.

Validated against a local https harness: cache holds exactly 8 under a
50-proxy rotation with FIFO eviction, a real CONNECT proxy still tunnels
(with and after eviction), 302 raises NetworkError on both direct and
proxied paths with a healthy pool afterwards, timeout/gzip paths
unchanged, and a 2,000-proxy rotation now retains 0.9MB post-GC vs
~46MB before.

* refactor(base): drop vendored proxy agents from static_dependencies

The native fetch transport handles httpProxy/httpsProxy/socksProxy
through undici dispatchers (getFetchProxyDispatcher), so the vendored
agent-base / http-proxy-agent / https-proxy-agent copies only backed the
legacy paths: user-supplied fetchImplementation functions and node-style
ws connection agents. Those paths now import the npm-installed
http-proxy-agent / https-proxy-agent / socks-proxy-agent packages
directly (the fallback loadProxyModules already had), and when a package
is missing they raise NotSupported with per-scheme install instructions,
matching the existing socks-proxy-agent behavior.

Behavioral note: ws-over-proxy and custom-fetchImplementation-over-proxy
users must "npm i http-proxy-agent https-proxy-agent" (or
socks-proxy-agent) themselves now - plain REST proxy usage through the
built-in transport is unaffected and needs no extra packages.

Generated js/dist copies of the vendored modules are left to the build
pipeline, same as the node-fetch removal earlier in this branch.

* docs(examples): migrate REST proxy examples from node-style agents to undici.ProxyAgent config

The custom-proxy-agent and proxy-usage examples still configured REST
proxying with the removed pattern (http-proxy-agent / https-proxy-agent
instances passed as 'agent' / 'httpsAgent'). They now show the two
supported shapes on the undici transport:

- simple: the unified httpProxy/httpsProxy/socksProxy properties, which
  build and cache an undici.ProxyAgent dispatcher internally
- advanced: injecting a custom-tuned undici.ProxyAgent into
  exchange.fetchProxyDispatchers[proxyUrl] (custom tls, proxy headers,
  pooling limits)

Both patterns are verified against a live CONNECT proxy (tunnel counted
server-side, custom dispatcher confirmed used via its dispatch hook).
The websocket snippet keeps the node-style agent, which ws connections
still require, with a note to npm-install the agent package. The
old-style 'agent' option remains documented as honored only by
user-supplied fetchImplementation functions.

* refactor(base): rename fetchProxyDispatchers to proxyDictionaries, matching master

The undici dispatcher cache now lives in the proxyDictionaries property
that master (and the legacy setProxyAgents path on this branch) already
uses, so the public surface carries one per-proxy-url cache name instead
of two. Both families share the dict keyed by plain proxy url and are
discriminated by the 'dispatch' method: getFetchProxyDispatcher only
returns/creates undici dispatchers, setProxyAgents only returns/creates
node-style agents, and a url switching families transparently recreates
the right handle.

The FIFO cap (renamed proxyDictionariesMaxSize, default 8) now guards
the shared dict through a common cacheProxyDictionary helper, extending
the rotating-proxy leak fix to the legacy agent path as well. Eviction
and family-switch replacement close undici dispatchers gracefully
(close () drains in-flight requests) but never destroy legacy agents,
matching master's never-destroy semantics and keeping live ws
connections on their agents intact.

Examples updated: custom dispatcher injection is now
exchange.proxyDictionaries[proxyUrl] = new ProxyAgent (...).

Validated live: 15/15 transport suite (proxying, redirect NetworkError,
cap, 0.9MB post-GC after 2,000 rotations), both example patterns, and 6
new shared-dict checks covering dispatcher/agent collision on the same
proxy url in both directions plus mixed-entry FIFO capping.

* build: move undici from optionalDependencies to dependencies

The native-fetch transport in this PR makes undici a hard runtime
requirement on node - a failed optional install must not produce a
broken client.

ecdsa static dependency, use coincurve + cryptography (#29131)

* Remove vendored ecdsa static dependency, use coincurve + cryptography

- Delete python/ccxt/static_dependencies/ecdsa (~3400 lines of vendored
  pure-python crypto)
- Exchange.ecdsa now uses coincurve for secp256k1 (with a cryptography
  fallback) and the cryptography library's deterministic RFC 6979
  signing for the NIST curves (p192/p224/p256/p384/p521)
- Signatures (r, s, v) are byte-for-byte identical to the previous
  implementation for all previously supported curve/hash combos
- Replace the fixed-length retry loop with native prehashed
  deterministic signing via cryptography
- Move the pure-python RFC 6979 helper into starkware/crypto for the
  STARK curve (not supported by OpenSSL) and keep pedersen hashing
  self-contained there

* pyproject: gate coincurve on CPython + prebuilt wheel availability

coincurve 21.0.0 only ships wheels for CPython 3.9-3.13 (no PyPy, no
cp314) on linux x86_64/aarch64/i686, macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows
AMD64/ARM64. Restrict the marker to that matrix so 'pip install ccxt'
never triggers a C source build; ccxt falls back to the cryptography
implementation when coincurve is absent. Also mirror the entry into the
dev extra. Note win32 needs an explicit != "x86" exclusion because
"x86" is a substring of "x86_64" under the 'in' marker operator.

* fix(build): drop space before paren in transpiled PHP (array()/max/min)

* chore(build): add php-cs-fixer (PSR-12) style check and emit space-free call parens

- add friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer as a composer require-dev + .php-cs-fixer.dist.php
  config (PSR-12 + array_syntax=long to keep array() everywhere, not [])
- add npm "check-php-style" (php-cs-fixer --dry-run gate, analogous to the python
  checks) and rename "check-python-ruff" -> "check-python-style" everywhere
  (package.json, python/package.json copy, .claude/settings.json + pr-reviewer agent)
- transpiler now emits PSR-12 no_spaces_after_function_name compliant calls:
  strip the space before "(" in ->/:: method calls (incl. implicit api calls,
  local-variable calls and dynamic $this->$method() calls), constructor calls
  (new Foo ()) and the async closure IIFE (})();)
- gitignore .php-cs-fixer.cache

* fix(build): drop --diff from check-php-style so it completes

php-cs-fixer --diff emitted ~530k lines / 26MB for the not-yet-reformatted
committed php tree (every method trips braces_position), flooding the
terminal so the script appeared to hang. Dry-run alone returns the same
pass/fail exit code in ~14s with bounded output; pass '-- --diff' ad hoc.

* chore(build): make transpiled exchange PHP pass php-cs-fixer (K&R) and scope the gate

Reconcile the php-cs-fixer gate with what the transpiler emits so regenerated
exchange files are style-clean:

- .php-cs-fixer.dist.php: enforce K&R / one-true-brace (same_line) instead of
  PSR-12 brace-on-next-line, keep array()=long, and scope the Finder to the
  generated exchange files only (php/<id>.php, php/async/<id>.php,
  php/pro/<id>.php; depth 0 + notName Uppercase) - excluding hand-written
  base/error classes, transpiled tests and auto-generated abstract signatures.
  Disable statement_indentation + ternary_operator_spaces (regex transpiler can't
  satisfy them for a few cosmetic cases).

- build/transpile.ts: emit PSR-12-compliant code -
  * no blank line after the class opening brace
  * use React\... imports without a leading backslash (no_leading_import_slash)
  * convert empty "[ ]" and one-level-nested "[ $x['key'] ]" arrays to array()
  * "[]" default in signatures -> array()
  * json_encode( / new $var[...]( / $this->prop->method( spacing, and the empty
    async closure no longer emits "function ()  {" (double space)
  * do NOT prefix the array()/list()/... construct call form when a method has a
    param named like the construct (e.g. filterBySinceLimit(array, ...), coinsph) -
    previously array() literals there were corrupted into $array().

- ts/src/bitfinex.ts: reword (comment-only) the sample-response comments inside the
  fetchMarkets labels array so they don't contain unbalanced [] that blocked the
  array()-conversion; array values are unchanged.

Result: npm run check-php-style is green (0 of 287 exchange files). Validated with
check-php-syntax and request/response tests (sync + async) for htx, binance,
bitfinex, coinsph, grvt.

* refactor(build): move objectPropertyMethodCall regex into getPHPRegexes

It only needs "$this->" (already produced inside getPHPRegexes via this.->$this->),
so it can live with the other PHP regexes instead of the final concat pass. Placed at
the end of getPHPRegexes, after the specific .slice/.split/.toUpperCase/... method
conversions, so it only catches leftover $this->prop.method( (e.g. $this->orders.append()).

noSpaceBeforeCallParen and noSpaceBeforeDynamicNewParen stay in the final pass: the
former needs local-variable "->" from variablePropertiesRegexes and the latter needs
the "$" from phpVariablesRegexes, both of which run after getPHPRegexes.

No output change: check-php-style still green (0/287); request/response (sync+async)
pass for htx, binance, bitfinex, coinsph, grvt.

* restore bitfinex

* ci(php): run check-php-style after transpilation

* move npm run copy-python-files to python.yml

This reverts commit 89bd5ba3b4228c9fa8832ebced3eddc0695e3a24.

include a tsc type-check step for CJS types.

bundler moduleResolution for Vite/Next.js/webpack users, and destructured
CJS require imports.

* refactor: move ccxt.d.cts to package root

Place CJS type declaration at the package root instead of dist/, avoiding
the unnecessary ../js/ relative path. Update .npmignore, package.json
exports map, and rollup config accordingly.

* refactor: rename ccxt.d.cts to index.d.cts

Keep the CJS type declaration filename consistent with the original
index.d.ts convention.

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="fix(build): drop space before paren in transpiled PHP (array()/max/min) (#29010)

* fix(build): drop space before paren in transpiled PHP (array()/max/min)

* chore(build): add php-cs-fixer (PSR-12) style check and emit space-free call parens

- add friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer as a composer require-dev + .php-cs-fixer.dist.php
  config (PSR-12 + array_syntax=long to keep array() everywhere, not [])
- add npm "check-php-style" (php-cs-fixer --dry-run gate, analogous to the python
  checks) and rename "check-python-ruff" -> "check-python-style" everywhere
  (package.json, python/package.json copy, .claude/settings.json + pr-reviewer agent)
- transpiler now emits PSR-12 no_spaces_after_function_name compliant calls:
  strip the space before "(" in ->/:: method calls (incl. implicit api calls,
  local-variable calls and dynamic $this->$method() calls), constructor calls
  (new Foo ()) and the async closure IIFE (})();)
- gitignore .php-cs-fixer.cache

* fix(build): drop --diff from check-php-style so it completes

php-cs-fixer --diff emitted ~530k lines / 26MB for the not-yet-reformatted
committed php tree (every method trips braces_position), flooding the
terminal so the script appeared to hang. Dry-run alone returns the same
pass/fail exit code in ~14s with bounded output; pass '-- --diff' ad hoc.

* chore(build): make transpiled exchange PHP pass php-cs-fixer (K&R) and scope the gate

Reconcile the php-cs-fixer gate with what the transpiler emits so regenerated
exchange files are style-clean:

- .php-cs-fixer.dist.php: enforce K&R / one-true-brace (same_line) instead of
  PSR-12 brace-on-next-line, keep array()=long, and scope the Finder to the
  generated exchange files only (php/<id>.php, php/async/<id>.php,
  php/pro/<id>.php; depth 0 + notName Uppercase) - excluding hand-written
  base/error classes, transpiled tests and auto-generated abstract signatures.
  Disable statement_indentation + ternary_operator_spaces (regex transpiler can't
  satisfy them for a few cosmetic cases).

- build/transpile.ts: emit PSR-12-compliant code -
  * no blank line after the class opening brace
  * use React\... imports without a leading backslash (no_leading_import_slash)
  * convert empty "[ ]" and one-level-nested "[ $x['key'] ]" arrays to array()
  * "[]" default in signatures -> array()
  * json_encode( / new $var[...]( / $this->prop->method( spacing, and the empty
    async closure no longer emits "function ()  {" (double space)
  * do NOT prefix the array()/list()/... construct call form when a method has a
    param named like the construct (e.g. filterBySinceLimit(array, ...), coinsph) -
    previously array() literals there were corrupted into $array().

- ts/src/bitfinex.ts: reword (comment-only) the sample-response comments inside the
  fetchMarkets labels array so they don't contain unbalanced [] that blocked the
  array()-conversion; array values are unchanged.

Result: npm run check-php-style is green (0 of 287 exchange files). Validated with
check-php-syntax and request/response tests (sync + async) for htx, binance,
bitfinex, coinsph, grvt.

* refactor(build): move objectPropertyMethodCall regex into getPHPRegexes

It only needs "$this->" (already produced inside getPHPRegexes via this.->$this->),
so it can live with the other PHP regexes instead of the final concat pass. Placed at
the end of getPHPRegexes, after the specific .slice/.split/.toUpperCase/... method
conversions, so it only catches leftover $this->prop.method( (e.g. $this->orders.append()).

noSpaceBeforeCallParen and noSpaceBeforeDynamicNewParen stay in the final pass: the
former needs local-variable "->" from variablePropertiesRegexes and the latter needs
the "$" from phpVariablesRegexes, both of which run after getPHPRegexes.

No output change: check-php-style still green (0/287); request/response (sync+async)
pass for htx, binance, bitfinex, coinsph, grvt.

* restore bitfinex

* fix(build): drop space before paren in transpiled PHP (array()/max/min)

* chore(build): add php-cs-fixer (PSR-12) style check and emit space-free call parens

- add friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer as a composer require-dev + .php-cs-fixer.dist.php
  config (PSR-12 + array_syntax=long to keep array() everywhere, not [])
- add npm "check-php-style" (php-cs-fixer --dry-run gate, analogous to the python
  checks) and rename "check-python-ruff" -> "check-python-style" everywhere
  (package.json, python/package.json copy, .claude/settings.json + pr-reviewer agent)
- transpiler now emits PSR-12 no_spaces_after_function_name compliant calls:
  strip the space before "(" in ->/:: method calls (incl. implicit api calls,
  local-variable calls and dynamic $this->$method() calls), constructor calls
  (new Foo ()) and the async closure IIFE (})();)
- gitignore .php-cs-fixer.cache

* fix(build): drop --diff from check-php-style so it completes

php-cs-fixer --diff emitted ~530k lines / 26MB for the not-yet-reformatted
committed php tree (every method trips braces_position), flooding the
terminal so the script appeared to hang. Dry-run alone returns the same
pass/fail exit code in ~14s with bounded output; pass '-- --diff' ad hoc.

* chore(build): make transpiled exchange PHP pass php-cs-fixer (K&R) and scope the gate

Reconcile the php-cs-fixer gate with what the transpiler emits so regenerated
exchange files are style-clean:

- .php-cs-fixer.dist.php: enforce K&R / one-true-brace (same_line) instead of
  PSR-12 brace-on-next-line, keep array()=long, and scope the Finder to the
  generated exchange files only (php/<id>.php, php/async/<id>.php,
  php/pro/<id>.php; depth 0 + notName Uppercase) - excluding hand-written
  base/error classes, transpiled tests and auto-generated abstract signatures.
  Disable statement_indentation + ternary_operator_spaces (regex transpiler can't
  satisfy them for a few cosmetic cases).

- build/transpile.ts: emit PSR-12-compliant code -
  * no blank line after the class opening brace
  * use React\... imports without a leading backslash (no_leading_import_slash)
  * convert empty "[ ]" and one-level-nested "[ $x['key'] ]" arrays to array()
  * "[]" default in signatures -> array()
  * json_encode( / new $var[...]( / $this->prop->method( spacing, and the empty
    async closure no longer emits "function ()  {" (double space)
  * do NOT prefix the array()/list()/... construct call form when a method has a
    param named like the construct (e.g. filterBySinceLimit(array, ...), coinsph) -
    previously array() literals there were corrupted into $array().

- ts/src/bitfinex.ts: reword (comment-only) the sample-response comments inside the
  fetchMarkets labels array so they don't contain unbalanced [] that blocked the
  array()-conversion; array values are unchanged.

Result: npm run check-php-style is green (0 of 287 exchange files). Validated with
check-php-syntax and request/response tests (sync + async) for htx, binance,
bitfinex, coinsph, grvt.

noSpaceBeforeCallParen and noSpaceBeforeDynamicNewParen stay in the final pass: the

the "$" from phpVariablesRegexes, both of which run after getPHPRegexes.

* feat(base): add typed overloads to safe* accessors for non-undefined defaults

Add overload signatures to safeDict/safeDict2/safeDictN/safeList/safeList2/safeListN
so that callers supplying a non-undefined defaultValue receive a non-undefined return
type, eliminating many TS18048 'possibly undefined' errors under strictNullChecks.

Teach the regex transpiler (build/transpile.ts) and AST transpilers
(csharp/go/java via build/stripOverloads.ts) to strip body-less TS overload
signature lines before transpiling, since they carry no runtime code.

* fix(rest): annotate sign() headers as NullableDict to fix TS18048

Type the headers parameter of derived exchange sign() methods as NullableDict
(matching the base Exchange.sign signature) so the 'headers !== undefined' narrowing
resolves the possibly-undefined member access under strictNullChecks.

* fix(rest): pass default values to safeDict/safeList to fix TS18048

Supply [] / {} defaults to safeList/safeDict/safeDictN calls whose result is
iterated or indexed without an undefined guard, leveraging the new typed overloads
so the return type is non-undefined under strictNullChecks.

* fix(rest): use safeString/safeBool for possibly-undefined market access

Replace direct market['key'] member access with this.safeString/this.safeBool in
parse helpers where the market parameter is possibly undefined, resolving TS18048
under strictNullChecks while preserving runtime behaviour.

* fix(build): repair py/php/java transpilation broken by safe* overloads

- Use NullableDict/NullableList (not Dictionary<any>|undefined / any[]|undefined) for
  the safe* implementation signatures so the regex transpiler emits valid PHP (?array)
  and Python (dict/List[Any]) instead of '?Dictionary<any> | null' / 'NullableList'.
- Map NullableList in build/transpile.ts (php ?array, python List[Any]).
- Strip overload signature lines in build/generateJavaWrappers.ts before the ast-transpiler
  parses base Exchange.ts (the standalone java-wrapper generator crashed on them).
- Extract safeBool into a local in xt/bybit parseOHLCV: the regex ternary transpiler
  cannot handle a function-call (comma) condition inside (cond) ? a : b.

* fix(rest): guard possibly-undefined headers in sign() before member writes

Initialize headers to {} when undefined on code paths that write header keys without
a prior assignment (bitbns www POST, bullish non-GET/POST, bybit POST broker, kucoin
after extend, mexc public POST), resolving TS18048 under strictNullChecks.

* feat(base): add typed overloads to marketIds/currencyIds

A defined string[] input now yields a non-undefined string[] return, fixing TS18048
at callers that join the result inside an 'if (symbols !== undefined)' guard. Overload
signatures are stripped before transpilation by the existing stripOverloads machinery.

* feat(base): add typed overload to marketSymbols

A defined symbols array now yields a non-undefined string[] return, propagating through
callers (marketIds(symbols).join, etc.) to fix TS18048 under strictNullChecks. Overload
signatures are stripped before transpilation by the existing stripOverloads machinery.
Add the overload param names to eslint argsIgnorePattern.

* fix(rest): guard this.ids and narrow marketIds in fetchOrderBooks (upbit, exmo)

Type the local ids as Str, guard the possibly-undefined this.ids before join, and rely

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="docs: add Fumadocs documentation site (#28726)

* docs: add Fumadocs documentation site

Next.js + Fumadocs static-export docs site under website/, fed by the existing generated wiki/*.md via build/wiki-to-fumadocs.ts (same source of truth). Docsify is untouched and runs in parallel.

- build/wiki-to-fumadocs.ts: convert wiki/*.md -> website/content/docs (links, docsify-tabs->tabs, anchors, descriptions)
- build/check-fumadocs-links.ts: internal link/anchor gate + baseline
- website/: static export, Orama search, language + sidebar tabs, sitemap/robots, image zoom
- package.json: fumadocs-content / fumadocs-regen / fumadocs-build / fumadocs-dev / fumadocs-linkcheck

* fix(docs): render remote images without next/image; drop broken links

- mdx.tsx: render a plain <img> inside ImageZoom so next/image's required width/height no longer crashes pages with dimensionless remote images (e.g. exchange-markets)
- converter: strip `](undefined)` links from generated markets pages
- link checker: ignore /_next and asset URLs (hashed chunks); refresh baseline

* ci(docs): add Fumadocs deploy workflow; support /v2 subpath build

- .github/workflows/docs-fumadocs.yml: on release/master-push/dispatch, convert committed wiki -> build -> rsync to the docs server (least-privilege: forks excluded, pinned host key, empty-build guard, concurrency).
- next.config basePath via NEXT_BASE_PATH; robots/sitemap/layout honor the subpath and noindex the /v2 staging build.

* fix(docs): make static search basePath-aware (fixes /v2 search)

Next doesn't prepend basePath to fetch(), so the static Orama client requested /api/search and missed the index under /v2. Pass a basePath-aware `from` (NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH + /api/search). Verified: 318 hits for 'binance', etc.

* docs(manuals): add missing language tabs (Go, C#) to Manual + Pro manual

Fills in Go and C#/.NET code in the multi-language tab blocks so every example covers all 6 languages (was missing Go in many, e.g. watchOrders; C#+Go in cancelOrderWs). Signatures/examples verified against the transpiled go/v4 and cs/ccxt sources. A few dynamic-only blocks (runtime method reassignment) intentionally left JS/Python-only.

Pre-existing (not changed): an unclosed tabs:start at the signIn block; a $lmit typo in the watchOrders PHP signature.

* fix(docs): make AI/LLM artifacts basePath-aware (page actions, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, content.md)

Like search, Next doesn't prepend basePath to these manually-built URLs, so on /v2 the Copy/View-Markdown buttons and llms links pointed at the root (old Docsify). Prefix basePath in getPageMarkdownUrl/getPageImage/getLLMText and the llms.txt index.

* feat(docs): run Fumadocs as a containerized Next.js server (not static export)

Switch from static export to a server build (output: standalone) deployed as a Docker container behind nginx at /v2 (reverse-proxy -> 127.0.0.1:3005, restart=always). Enables the framework-native server features and drops the static-export constraints.

- next.config: output standalone (NEXT_OUTPUT=export still available); pin outputFileTracingRoot.
- website/Dockerfile + .dockerignore: multi-stage standalone image.
- package.json: start -> next start (start:static kept for the export).
- docs-fumadocs.yml: build arm64 image -> GHCR -> box pulls + restarts the container (was static rsync).

Note: GHCR-based deploy needs the existing DOCS_DEPLOY_* secrets; the box is arm64 so CI builds on an arm64 runner. Server is already live/manual on the box; the workflow automates redeploys.

* feat(docs): on-demand rendering + AI markdown endpoints (.md / Accept), metadataBase

- Render docs/og/llms routes on demand (drop generateStaticParams) + cache (revalidate=false): image 1.6GB -> ~540MB (no baked pages).
- .md URLs (/docs/x.md) via next.config rewrites + Accept: text/markdown via middleware -> the markdown route; route strips the content.md suffix only when present.
- metadataBase = siteUrl (fixes the localhost OG warning); basePath read from build-inlined NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH so runtime URLs keep /v2.

* feat(docs): add Ask-AI chat to Fumadocs site

Wires an "Ask AI" assistant into the /v2 Fumadocs docs:

- /api/chat route (OpenRouter via @openrouter/ai-sdk-provider + ai SDK)
  with a FlexSearch-backed `search` tool that grounds answers in the docs
  and cites source URLs.
- AISearch trigger in the docs layout, gated on NEXT_PUBLIC_AI_ENABLED so
  it only shows when AI is built in.
- Default model inclusionai/ling-2.6-flash (cheapest tool-capable model;
  free models are blocked by OpenRouter account data policy). Overridable
  at runtime via OPENROUTER_MODEL.

The OPENROUTER_API_KEY is provided only at runtime (root-only env-file on
the box, never baked into the image or stored in GitHub). The deploy
workflow injects that env-file on each redeploy so Ask-AI survives.

* fix(docs): trim Ask-AI search results and disable model reasoning leak

- The search tool returned enriched docs verbatim; on CCXT's huge per-exchange
  pages a single call could exceed 700k tokens and overflow the model context.
  Cap to 6 results and snippet each page's content to 1200 chars.
- Disable extended thinking via providerOptions.openrouter.reasoning.enabled=false
  so hybrid reasoning models (e.g. GLM) don't stream their chain-of-thought into
  the answer. No-op for plain instruct models.

* feat(docs): clearer multi-section nav + harden .dockerignore

- Promote the three root sections to always-visible sidebar tabs via
  tabMode="top" (was a buried dropdown that just said "Exchanges", making
  it hard to jump between Guide/Exchanges/Examples). Add icon + description
  to each root meta.json and resolve icon strings to Lucide components in
  source.ts. Rename the guide root tab "CCXT" -> "Guide" so Install/manual
  is an obvious one-click destination from any exchange/example page.
- .dockerignore/.gitignore: exclude .env / .env.* so a stray local env file
  can never be COPY . .'d into the image.

* fix(docs): remove tabMode="top" — it blanked all doc pages

Fumadocs renders its top "LayoutTabs" bar into the SAME CSS grid cell as
the page article ([grid-area:main]); the bar carries z-10 + an opaque
bg-fd-background and stretches to fill the cell, so it painted over and
completely hid the article on every docs page (the content was in the DOM
but invisible). Reverting to the default tabMode (auto) renders the root
sections as a sidebar switcher instead and restores the content. The
icon/description/"Guide" labels from the previous commit are kept, so the
switcher is still clearer than the original bare dropdown.

* feat(docs): animated homepage hero showcasing CCXT

Replace the placeholder homepage with a "Change one word -> connect to any
exchange" hero: an animated code-swap that cycles a CCXT fetchTicker snippet
across exchanges and languages (TS/Python/PHP/Go/C#/Java) beside a live unified-
response card, plus an exchange picker. Inline-SVG CCXT mark (themes itself),
respects prefers-reduced-motion, ARIA tablist. Keeps the six doc-entry cards.
Dockerfile now copies website/public so the bundled assets serve under /v2.

* feat(docs): harden Ask-AI chat, clearer section nav, link/SEO cleanup

Ask-AI chat (/api/chat):
- Abuse caps for the public endpoint: Zod body validation (<=40 messages,
  <=32KB), 400/413 on bad/oversized, 503 when the key is unset, same-origin
  guard. Pairs with the nginx per-IP limit_req scoped to /v2/api/chat only.
- maxDuration=30 + AbortSignal.timeout(28s) so a stalled free model can't hold
  a worker open.
- Observability: onFinish logs model/tokens/finishReason; onError logs server-
  side and returns a friendly, actionable message instead of "An error occurred."
- Reliability: OpenRouter `models` fallback chain (free primary -> near-free
  paid) so a flapping free model doesn't kill the chat.
- Prompt guardrail: treat search results / client context as untrusted data.
- Smaller in-memory index: cap page content to 12KB and skip example bodies.

Navigation:
- Always-visible Guide / Exchanges / Examples navbar links so you can cross
  between sections from any page (the sidebar root switcher alone wasn't obvious).
- "Ask AI" button gated on the OpenRouter key being present at runtime, not just
  the build flag -- no more show-then-fail.

Cleanup:
- "View source" links point at the real wiki/*.md on master (the previous
  content/docs path was gitignored/generated -> 404).
- robots.ts / sitemap.ts use the build-inlined NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH like the
  rest of the app (NEXT_BASE_PATH isn't defined at runtime).

* ci(docs): canary smoke-test deploy with auto-abort

Tag images by SHA and validate the new image on a temp port BEFORE swapping the
live container -- assert real rendered output (binance article present, no
duplicated [grid-area:main] overlap, no error boundary, homepage hero) rather
than just HTTP 200 (today's blank-page regression returned 200). If smoke fails,
the live container is left untouched and the job fails -- no downtime, no bad
deploy.

* feat(docs): hero beam + homepage install commands

- Restore the "beam": a brand-colored glowing line + traveling comet drawn
  from the active exchange chip up to the swapping token in the code, tracking
  swaps/typing/theme/resize each frame (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion).
- Remove the "Auto-cycling · click any exchange to swap" hint.
- Add an "Install in seconds" block: an AI-agent one-liner
  (install-skills.sh) plus per-language install commands
  (npm / pip / composer / dotnet / go get / gradle) with click-to-copy.

* feat(docs): add C#/Go/Java code examples

The example sections only covered JS/Python/TS/PHP. The C#/Go/Java sources
existed but in different layouts (C# under examples/cs/examples, Go flat in
examples/go, Java nested in java/examples/src), and the generator was grabbing
project files (c#.csproj/.sln) — which also broke the MDX build on the "#".

Refactor examples2md.js to take an explicit source dir + extension filter
(skips .csproj/.sln/.gradle.kts) + recursion (Java), and add cs/go/java to the
wiki-to-fumadocs converter. Adds C# (33), Go (11) and Java (21) example pages,
syntax-highlighted, in the Examples sidebar. JS/Python/TS/PHP output unchanged.

* fix(docs): remove redundant sidebar root-switcher dropdown

The sidebar showed Fumadocs' root-toggle dropdown (e.g. just "Exchanges") right
above the Guide/Exchanges/Examples navbar links that already switch sections —
a confusing one-option control. Set tabs={false}; the sidebar still scopes to
the active section by URL and the navbar links handle switching.

* fix(docs): drop stray "exchanges", add examples landing + changelog card

- Exchanges sidebar listed fetchCurrencies/fetchBidsAsks/fetchStatus — stray
  0-byte files in wiki/exchanges that aren't exchanges. Filter 0-byte files in
  exchangeOrder() (durable) and remove the three tracked empties.
- /docs/examples used to 404 and the nav jumped straight to /docs/examples/js.
  Generate an examples landing page (a per-language chooser) and point the
  Examples navbar link + homepage card at /docs/examples.
- Add a Changelog card to the homepage.

* fix(docs): address PR review — homepage SEO/OG, a11y, install + beam fixes

- Homepage now has a <title>, description and an OG/social image
  (/og/home, basePath-aware) — previously a blank tab title + imageless preview.
- Fix the Java install one-liner (cd into ccxt/java before ./gradlew).
- Add a "view script" link next to the AI `curl … | bash` one-liner.
- Tab widgets (exchange picker, language tabs, install tabs) were role="tab"
  without keyboard/tabpanel support — switch to honest buttons + aria-pressed,
  and announce copy success via an aria-live region.
- Pause the hero auto-cycle on hover/keyboard focus (WCAG 2.2.2).
- Beam rAF now skips its per-frame layout work when the tab is hidden, the hero
  is scrolled off-screen, or on mobile (where the beam is hidden) — via
  IntersectionObserver + a matchMedia guard.
- Reuse gitConfig for the GitHub link instead of a hardcoded URL.

* chore(docs): regenerate example pages — clean titles, drop self-link bullet

Each generated example page opened with a stray, mis-cased self-link bullet
(e.g. "- [Fetchohlcv](/docs/examples/go)") above the code. Drop that line and
fix the title-casing so acronym/camelCase filenames stay readable
(fetchOHLCV -> FetchOHLCV, not Fetchohlcv). Regenerates all language examples.

* feat(docs): examples landing as a card grid with language logos

Replace the plain bullet-list chooser at /docs/examples with a card grid
(brand logos via react-icons, tinted per language). Rendered by overriding the
exact /docs/examples path in the docs catch-all route — the generated
examples/index.md stays for the sidebar entry, the .md endpoint and metadata.
Per-language example pages and links are unchanged.

* feat(docs): add CCXT logo mark next to the navbar/sidebar title

Render the inline CcxtMark before the "CCXT" wordmark in the layout nav title
(themes via currentColor; shows in both the home navbar and the docs sidebar header).

* feat(docs): Ask-AI on homepage, gradle Java install, hero polish

- Add the "Ask AI" widget to the homepage layout so visitors can try it right
  away (gated on the build flag — the home page is static, so it can't read the
  runtime key; the /api/chat route still 503s safely if the key is missing).
- Java install now shows the Maven Central gradle dependency
  (implementation("io.github.ccxt:ccxt:4.5.56")) instead of a git clone; the
  install line drops the "$" prompt for non-shell snippets.
- Hero: tighten the top whitespace and invert the heading emphasis so
  "Connect to any exchange." is the bright line and "Change one word." is muted.

* feat(docs): default Ask-AI to openrouter/free model router

Use OpenRouter's free-model router (openrouter/free) as the default chat model —
it randomly selects a free model that supports the request's features (incl.
tool calling, which the docs `search` tool requires), avoiding any single free
model's "no healthy upstream" flapping. Live model is set via OPENROUTER_MODEL
on the box; near-free paid fallback (ling) kept as last resort.

* perf(docs): lazy-load doc images

Doc pages embed many remote badges/screenshots with no intrinsic dimensions.
Add loading="lazy" + decoding="async" to the MDX <img> so image-heavy pages
(e.g. the manual, 400+ images) don't fetch them all eagerly — cuts layout
shift and on-load network.

* docs(website): rewrite the stale README

Was the generic Create-Fumadocs scaffold claiming "Static Export configured" —
the app is a standalone Node server (containerized). Document the real setup:
the wiki -> converter -> content/docs pipeline, local dev, the /v2 basePath,
key files, and the containerized deploy.

* fix(docs): read Java install version from the repo, not hardcoded

The homepage Java/gradle line pinned "4.5.56". The wiki converter now writes the
root package.json version to website/src/lib/ccxt-version.json, and the install
component reads it — so the gradle dependency line stays current automatically
(the converter runs before every build, incl. CI).

* fix(docs): strip empty docsify anchors that broke #fragment links

Exchange/manual pages carried leftover docsify anchors `<a name="X" id="x"></a>`
right before each `### X` heading. Fumadocs already gives the heading that id, so
these created DUPLICATE ids — and `#fragment` navigation jumped to the empty,
scroll-margin-less anchor instead of the heading (e.g. clicking cancelAllOrders
on an exchange page didn't land on the section). Strip them in the converter;
the heading id (with scroll-margin) is now the single, correct target.

* fix(docs): keep the Ask-AI panel below the home navbar (was clipped)

On the home layout the Ask-AI panel falls back to lg:top-0 (its grid-area:toc
placement only applies in the docs/notebook layouts), so its header sat behind
the sticky h-14 z-40 navbar and got clipped. Offset the panel to start below the
navbar (top:3.5rem, height:calc(100dvh-3.5rem)) on #nd-home-layout only.

* fix(docs): render optional method params as 'name?' not '[, name]'

methodSig() in wiki/helpers.cjs wrapped trailing optional params in a
single grouped bracket — createOrder (symbol, type, side, amount[, price,
params]) — and even emitted a stray empty bracket (params[]) when nothing
was optional. Render each optional param with a trailing '?' instead:
createOrder (symbol, type, side, amount, price?, params?), which reads as
a normal language signature. Migrated the 103 affected exchange pages.

* fix(docs): drop removed-exchange pages and dead links from the site

jsdoc2md never deletes wiki pages for removed exchanges and misnames
pages for inheritance-only exchanges, so wiki/exchanges/ accumulates
orphan pages (probit, oxfun, okcoin, timex, zonda, alp) and stray
method-name pages (fetchBidsAsks, fetchCurrencies, fetchStatus). The
fumadocs converter now emits an exchange page only when ts/src/<id>.ts
exists, and unlinks references to removed exchanges so the baseSpec
method-support index no longer 404s. Self-corrects on every build.

* fix(docs): use the official boxed CCXT logo (theme-adaptive)

The navbar and hero pill showed bare CC/XT glyphs in the text colour with
no box. Render the official boxed mark instead: a filled currentColor
square with the glyphs knocked out in the page background, so it shows a
dark box with light glyphs in light mode and inverts to a light box with
dark glyphs in dark mode — one asset covers both themes. Drops the home
page's manual bg-black wrapper, now redundant.

* fix(docs): match the official CCXT logo glyphs exactly + add favicon

The boxed mark's glyphs didn't match the official: the X was 5 sparse 8px
dots and the box was rounded. Trace it 1:1 from the official 9x9 grid —
full 10-unit glyph cells (bolder CC/T strokes), a proper 3x3 checkerboard
X, and a sharp box. Add an adaptive SVG favicon (app/icon.svg) using the
same mark, following the browser's prefers-color-scheme.

* feat(docs): internationalize the site (en + es/pt/ko/zh/fr/de)

Add Fumadocs i18n: locale routing under /[lang] (English keeps the un-prefixed
/docs/... URLs, the other 6 locales are served at /<locale>/docs/...), a navbar
language switcher, and translated UI chrome (search, TOC, theme/language toggles,
pager, 404) for Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Chinese, French and German.

Generated reference content (exchanges, examples, API spec) falls back to English;
the hand-written guides are translated per-locale in a follow-up. proxy.ts merges
the locale-routing middleware with the existing markdown content-negotiation.
Search indexes the default locale only (the reference content is English across
every locale) to keep the static Orama index small.

* fix(docs): serve the i18n home at the basePath root (was a 404)

Two issues with locale routing under basePath (/v2):
- the proxy matcher's negative-lookahead pattern doesn't match the bare root, so
  the home never hit the middleware — add '/' to the matcher explicitly.
- the i18n middleware rewrites /docs -> /<default>/docs but leaves the root
  untouched, so the default-locale home 404s — rewrite '/' to the default-locale
  home in the proxy.
Also drop the [lang] generateStaticParams so the home renders on demand (like the
docs), avoiding a prerendered /<locale> home that redirects under hideLocale.

* feat(docs): translate the homepage + guide pages into 6 languages

The OPENROUTER_API_KEY is provided only at runtime (root-only env-file on

workflow injects that env-file on each redeploy so Ask-AI survives.

jsdoc2md.js named each wiki/exchanges/<name>.md from templateData[i][0].name,
assuming the first doclet is always the class. Exchange files that lack a
/** @class <id> @augments <Parent> */ comment produce no class doclet, so [0]
fell through to the first documented method: the page was written as an empty
phantom exchanges/<method>.md and the real page was dropped. Exchanges sharing
a first method collapsed onto the same name (last writer wins), so only a few
method-named files ever showed up:

  aftermath      (never had @class)              -> fetchCurrencies.md
  kucoinfutures  (lost @class in kucoin #27661)  -> fetchBidsAsks.md
  zebpay         (had a nameless `@class`)        -> fetchStatus.md

- restore the class-level doc-comment on the three exchange files
- jsdoc2md.js: derive the output filename from the source path (robust to
  doclet order); throw loudly when an exchange has no class-level doclet;
  remove stale per-exchange pages before regenerating; de-dup doclets per

title="refactor(pro): drop vendored fflate, use node:zlib in node with fflate fallback (#29014)

* refactor(pro): drop vendored fflate, use node:zlib in node with fflate fallback

Remove the ~2.5k-line vendored fflate copy under ts/src/static_dependencies/fflake/ and add fflate as a normal npm dependency. The WebSocket base Client.ts now prefers Node's built-in node:zlib when running under Node (gunzipSync for gzip exchanges, inflateRawSync for raw-deflate exchanges like bitmart), falling back to the fflate npm package in browser/other runtimes. node:zlib is lazily loaded via dynamic import with a webpackIgnore comment, mirroring io.ts. Client.ts is JS/TS-only, so no cross-language transpile is required.

* refactor(pro): pin fflate to 0.8.3 and load it only in the browser

Pin fflate to an exact version (0.8.3) and move it from dependencies to optionalDependencies. Client.ts no longer statically imports fflate; instead it lazily loads node:zlib under Node and the fflate npm package only in non-Node (browser) runtimes via a browser-only dynamic import (webpackMode eager so it is bundled into the main browser chunk, not fetched as a separate chunk). fflate is therefore never loaded or bundled in Node builds, where node:zlib handles decompression (gunzipSync for gzip exchanges, inflateRawSync for raw-deflate exchanges like bitmart). Kept fflate in rollup externals so the dynamic import stays external in the CJS build and is never pulled into Node output.

* fix(pro): regenerate WS Client to drop dangling vendored fflate import

The previous commits deleted the vendored fflate copy (ts/src/static_dependencies/fflake) and its generated mirrors, but the stale generated js/src/base/ws/Client.js and dist/cjs/src/base/ws/Client.js still imported '../../static_dependencies/fflake/browser.js'. Since that file was removed, loading js/ccxt.js failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which broke build/transpileWS.ts (it imports ../js/ccxt.js) and any CJS consumer of dist/cjs. Regenerated both Client.js files (tsc + addJsHeaders for js/, rollup for dist/cjs) so they use the npm fflate package + node:zlib and no longer reference the deleted vendored path. The committed browser bundle (dist/ccxt.browser*.js) and its stale source-map metadata are left to be regenerated by CI on merge; they inline the old code but contain no dangling import.

* perf(pro): resolve WS decompression backend once at startup

Instead of branching on isNode for every compressed frame in onMessage(), resolve the gunzip/inflate functions a single time when the lazy backend import settles: node:zlib's gunzipSync/inflateRawSync under Node, fflate's gunzipSync/inflateSync in the browser. The message hot path now just calls gunzipSync()/inflateRawSync() with no per-message conditional. Regenerated js/ and dist/cjs Client accordingly.

* refactor(pro): scope rollup interop to drop _interopNamespace from WS Client

node:zlib and fflate expose named exports directly on module.exports, so the
CJS bundle requires them bare instead of going through the interop helper.
Everything else keeps the legacy interop (true) so no other output changes.
dist/cjs is left to the automated build.

* chore: restore dist/ and js/ from master

Generated files are left to the automated build; this PR now only carries
source (ts/) and build-config changes.

* Remove vendored ecdsa static dependency, use coincurve + cryptography

- Delete python/ccxt/static_dependencies/ecdsa (~3400 lines of vendored
  pure-python crypto)
- Exchange.ecdsa now uses coincurve for secp256k1 (with a cryptography
  fallback) and the cryptography library's deterministic RFC 6979
  signing for the NIST curves (p192/p224/p256/p384/p521)
- Signatures (r, s, v) are byte-for-byte identical to the previous
  implementation for all previously supported curve/hash combos
- Replace the fixed-length retry loop with native prehashed
  deterministic signing via cryptography
- Move the pure-python RFC 6979 helper into starkware/crypto for the
  STARK curve (not supported by OpenSSL) and keep pedersen hashing
  self-contained there

* pyproject: gate coincurve on CPython + prebuilt wheel availability

coincurve 21.0.0 only ships wheels for CPython 3.9-3.13 (no PyPy, no
cp314) on linux x86_64/aarch64/i686, macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows
AMD64/ARM64. Restrict the marker to that matrix so 'pip install ccxt'
never triggers a C source build; ccxt falls back to the cryptography
implementation when coincurve is absent. Also mirror the entry into the
dev extra. Note win32 needs an explicit != "x86" exclusion because
"x86" is a substring of "x86_64" under the 'in' marker operator.

title="refactor(pro): drop vendored fflate, use node:zlib in node with fflate fallback (#29014)

* refactor(pro): drop vendored fflate, use node:zlib in node with fflate fallback

Remove the ~2.5k-line vendored fflate copy under ts/src/static_dependencies/fflake/ and add fflate as a normal npm dependency. The WebSocket base Client.ts now prefers Node's built-in node:zlib when running under Node (gunzipSync for gzip exchanges, inflateRawSync for raw-deflate exchanges like bitmart), falling back to the fflate npm package in browser/other runtimes. node:zlib is lazily loaded via dynamic import with a webpackIgnore comment, mirroring io.ts. Client.ts is JS/TS-only, so no cross-language transpile is required.

* refactor(pro): pin fflate to 0.8.3 and load it only in the browser

Pin fflate to an exact version (0.8.3) and move it from dependencies to optionalDependencies. Client.ts no longer statically imports fflate; instead it lazily loads node:zlib under Node and the fflate npm package only in non-Node (browser) runtimes via a browser-only dynamic import (webpackMode eager so it is bundled into the main browser chunk, not fetched as a separate chunk). fflate is therefore never loaded or bundled in Node builds, where node:zlib handles decompression (gunzipSync for gzip exchanges, inflateRawSync for raw-deflate exchanges like bitmart). Kept fflate in rollup externals so the dynamic import stays external in the CJS build and is never pulled into Node output.

* fix(pro): regenerate WS Client to drop dangling vendored fflate import

The previous commits deleted the vendored fflate copy (ts/src/static_dependencies/fflake) and its generated mirrors, but the stale generated js/src/base/ws/Client.js and dist/cjs/src/base/ws/Client.js still imported '../../static_dependencies/fflake/browser.js'. Since that file was removed, loading js/ccxt.js failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, which broke build/transpileWS.ts (it imports ../js/ccxt.js) and any CJS consumer of dist/cjs. Regenerated both Client.js files (tsc + addJsHeaders for js/, rollup for dist/cjs) so they use the npm fflate package + node:zlib and no longer reference the deleted vendored path. The committed browser bundle (dist/ccxt.browser*.js) and its stale source-map metadata are left to be regenerated by CI on merge; they inline the old code but contain no dangling import.

* perf(pro): resolve WS decompression backend once at startup

Instead of branching on isNode for every compressed frame in onMessage(), resolve the gunzip/inflate functions a single time when the lazy backend import settles: node:zlib's gunzipSync/inflateRawSync under Node, fflate's gunzipSync/inflateSync in the browser. The message hot path now just calls gunzipSync()/inflateRawSync() with no per-message conditional. Regenerated js/ and dist/cjs Client accordingly.

* refactor(pro): scope rollup interop to drop _interopNamespace from WS Client

node:zlib and fflate expose named exports directly on module.exports, so the
CJS bundle requires them bare instead of going through the interop helper.
Everything else keeps the legacy interop (true) so no other output changes.
dist/cjs is left to the automated build.

* chore: restore dist/ and js/ from master

Generated files are left to the automated build; this PR now only carries
source (ts/) and build-config changes.

<p dir="auto">The <strong>CCXT</strong> library is used to connect and trade with cryptocurrency exchanges worldwide. It provides quick access to market data for storage, analysis, visualization, indicator development, algorithmic trading, strategy backtesting, bot programming, and related software engineering.</p>
<p dir="auto">It is intended to be used by <strong>coders, developers, technically-skilled traders, data-scientists and financial analysts</strong> for building trading algorithms.</p>
<p dir="auto">Current feature list:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>supports many cryptocurrency exchanges — more coming soon</li>
<li>implements public and private APIs, both REST and WebSocket</li>
<li>optionally normalizes data for cross-exchange analytics and arbitrage</li>
<li>has an out of the box unified API that is extremely easy to integrate</li>
<li>ideal for AI agents and vibe coding</li>
<li>works in Node 18+, Python 3, PHP 8.1+, netstandard2.0/2.1, Go 1.20+, Java 21+ and web browsers</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">CCXT participates in builder programs with the exchanges listed above, which means that in order to support the CCXT project users pay a small fee (1 bps) on top of the exchanges' fees when using the exchanges' API through CCXT. This is optional and can be disabled by setting <code>exchange.options['builderFee'] = False</code>. For all other exchanges no additional fee is charged and in some cases you receive discounts or special conditions by using CCXT.</p>

<p dir="auto">The easiest way to install the CCXT library is to use a package manager:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><a href="https://www.npmjs.com/package/ccxt" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>NPM</strong></a> (JavaScript / Node v7.6+)</li>
<li><a href="https://pypi.python.org/pypi/ccxt" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>PyPI</strong></a> (Python 3.7.0+)</li>
<li><a href="https://packagist.org/packages/ccxt/ccxt" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>Packagist/Composer</strong></a> (PHP 8.1+)</li>
<li><a href="https://www.nuget.org/packages/ccxt" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>Nuget</strong></a> (netstandard 2.0)</li>
<li><a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/ccxt/ccxt/go/v4" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>GO</strong></a></li>
<li><a href="https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/io.github.ccxt/ccxt" rel="nofollow">ccxt in <strong>Java</strong></a> (Java 21+, Gradle)</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This library is shipped as an all-in-one module implementation with minimalistic dependencies and requirements:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">orjson support</h4><a id="user-content-orjson-support" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: orjson support" href="#orjson-support"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">CCXT also supports <code>orjson</code> for parsing JSON since it is much faster than the builtin library. This is especially important when using websockets because some exchanges return big messages that need to be parsed and dispatched as quickly as possible.</p>
<p dir="auto">However, <code>orjson</code> is not enabled by default because it is not supported by every python interpreter. If you want to opt-in, you just need to install it (<code>pip install orjson</code>) on your local environment. CCXT will detect the installion and pick it up automatically.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">ECDSA Support</h4><a id="user-content-ecdsa-support" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: ECDSA Support" href="#ecdsa-support"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Some exchanges, such as Hyperliquid, Binance, and Paradex use <strong>ECDSA</strong> for request signing.
By default, CCXT includes a pure Python ECDSA implementation that ensures compatibility across all environments. However, this implementation may not meet the performance requirements of latency-sensitive applications.</p>
<p dir="auto">To address this, CCXT also supports the Coincurve library, which dramatically reduces signing time from approximately 45 ms to under 0.05 ms.</p>
<p dir="auto">For optimal performance, we recommend installing Coincurve via:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto"><pre class="notranslate"><code>pip install coincurve
</code></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">Each exchange has its own typed subclass with strongly-typed return values. Every typed method ships both a blocking sync and a non-blocking <code>CompletableFuture</code>-returning async overload — pick the idiom that fits your call site:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-java notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c">// Sync — blocks until the response arrives</span>
<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span> <span class="pl-s1">ticker</span> = <span class="pl-s1">exchange</span>.<span class="pl-en">fetchTicker</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>);

<span class="pl-c">// Async — returns immediately, completes when the response arrives</span>
<span class="pl-smi">CompletableFuture</span><<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span>> <span class="pl-s1">future</span> = <span class="pl-s1">exchange</span>.<span class="pl-en">fetchTickerAsync</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">null</span>);
<span class="pl-s1">future</span>.<span class="pl-en">thenAccept</span>(<span class="pl-s1">t</span> -> <span class="pl-smi">System</span>.<span class="pl-s1">out</span>.<span class="pl-en">println</span>(<span class="pl-s1">t</span>.<span class="pl-s1">last</span>));</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="// Sync — blocks until the response arrives
Ticker ticker = exchange.fetchTicker("BTC/USDT");

// Async — returns immediately, completes when the response arrives
CompletableFuture<Ticker> future = exchange.fetchTickerAsync("BTC/USDT", null);
future.thenAccept(t -> System.out.println(t.last));" tabindex="0" role="button">

<p dir="auto">WebSocket support is available via the pro exchange classes, with the same sync/async symmetry — <code>watchTicker</code> blocks for one update; <code>watchTickerAsync</code> returns a <code>CompletableFuture<Ticker></code> you can compose:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-java notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">io</span>.<span class="pl-s1">github</span>.<span class="pl-s1">ccxt</span>.<span class="pl-s1">exchanges</span>.<span class="pl-s1">pro</span>.<span class="pl-s1">Binance</span>;

<span class="pl-smi">var</span> <span class="pl-s1">exchange</span> = <span class="pl-k">new</span> <span class="pl-smi">Binance</span>();
<span class="pl-s1">exchange</span>.<span class="pl-en">loadMarkets</span>(<span class="pl-c1">false</span>);

<span class="pl-c">// Sync — blocks for one update</span>
<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span> <span class="pl-s1">tick</span> = <span class="pl-s1">exchange</span>.<span class="pl-en">watchTicker</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>);

<span class="pl-c">// Async — returns a typed CompletableFuture (composable with allOf, anyOf, etc.)</span>
<span class="pl-smi">CompletableFuture</span><<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span>> <span class="pl-s1">future</span> = <span class="pl-s1">exchange</span>.<span class="pl-en">watchTickerAsync</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">null</span>);</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">The CCXT library consists of a public part and a private part. Anyone can use the public part immediately after installation. Public APIs provide unrestricted access to public information for all exchange markets without the need to register a user account or have an API key.</p>
<p dir="auto">Public APIs include the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>market data</li>
<li>instruments/trading pairs</li>
<li>price feeds (exchange rates)</li>
<li>order books</li>
<li>trade history</li>
<li>tickers</li>
<li>OHLC(V) for charting</li>
<li>other public endpoints</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">In order to trade with private APIs you need to obtain API keys from an exchange's website. It usually means signing up to the exchange and creating API keys for your account. Some exchanges require personal info or identification. Sometimes verification may be necessary as well. In this case you will need to register yourself, this library will not create accounts or API keys for you. Some exchanges expose API endpoints for registering an account, but most exchanges don't. You will have to sign up and create API keys on their websites.</p>
<p dir="auto">Private APIs allow the following:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>manage personal account info</li>
<li>query account balances</li>
<li>trade by making market and limit orders</li>
<li>deposit and withdraw fiat and crypto funds</li>
<li>query personal orders</li>
<li>get ledger history</li>
<li>transfer funds between accounts</li>
<li>use merchant services</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">This library implements full public and private REST and WebSocket APIs for all exchanges in TypeScript, JavaScript, PHP and Python.</p>
<p dir="auto">The CCXT library supports both camelcase notation (preferred in TypeScript and JavaScript) and underscore notation (preferred in Python and PHP), therefore all methods can be called in either notation or coding style in any language.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-js notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c">// both of these notations work in JavaScript/Python/PHP</span>
<span class="pl-s1">exchange</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-en">methodName</span> <span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span>  <span class="pl-c">// camelcase pseudocode</span>
<span class="pl-s1">exchange</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-en">method_name</span> <span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span> <span class="pl-c">// underscore pseudocode</span></pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

    <span class="pl-k">const</span> <span class="pl-s1">exchangeId</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s">'binance'</span>
        <span class="pl-kos">,</span> <span class="pl-s1">exchangeClass</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">ccxt</span><span class="pl-kos">[</span><span class="pl-s1">exchangeId</span><span class="pl-kos">]</span>

import (
	"github.com/ccxt/ccxt/go/v4/go"
	"fmt"
)

func main() {
	exchange := ccxt.NewBinance(map[string]interface{}{
		"apiKey": "MY KEY",
		"secret": "MY SECRET",
	})
	orderParams := map[string]interface{}{
		"clientOrderId": "myOrderId68768678",
	}

    exchange.LoadMarkets()

	order, err := exchange.CreateOrder("BTC/USDT", "limit", "buy", 0.001, ccxt.WithCreateOrderPrice(6000), ccxt.WithCreateOrderParams(orderParams))
	if err != nil {
		if ccxtError, ok := err.(*ccxt.Error); ok {
			if ccxtError.Type == "InvalidOrder" {
				fmt.Println("Invalid order")
			} else {
				fmt.Println("Some other error")
			}
		}
	} else {
		fmt.Println(*order.Id)
	}


    // fetching OHLCV
	ohlcv, err := exchange.FetchOHLCV("BTC/USDT", ccxt.WithFetchOHLCVTimeframe("5m"), ccxt.WithFetchOHLCVLimit(100))

	if err != nil {
		fmt.Println("Error: ", err)
	} else {
		fmt.Println("Got OHLCV!")
	}
}" tabindex="0" role="button">

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Optional parameters</h4><a id="user-content-optional-parameters" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Optional parameters" href="#optional-parameters"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Unlike Javascript/Python/PHP/C# Go does not support "traditional" optional parameters like <code>function a(optional = false)</code>. However, the CCXT language and structure have some methods with optional params, and since the Go language is transpiled from the Typescript source, we had to find a way of representing them.</p>
<p dir="auto">We have decided to "go" (pun intended) with Option structs and the <code>WithX</code> methods.</p>
<p dir="auto">For example, this function <code>FetchMyTrades</code> supports 4 different "optional" parameters, symbol, since, limit, and params.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-go notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">func</span> (<span class="pl-s1">this</span> <span class="pl-c1">*</span><span class="pl-smi">Binance</span>) <span class="pl-c1">FetchMyTrades</span>(<span class="pl-s1">options</span> <span class="pl-c1">...</span><span class="pl-smi">FetchMyTradesOptions</span>) ([]<span class="pl-smi">Trade</span>, <span class="pl-smi">error</span>)</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">Lastly, just because the signature dictates that some argument like <code>symbol</code> is optional, it will depend from exchange to exchange and you might need to provide it to avoid getting a <code>SymbolRequired</code> error.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can check different examples in the <code>examples/go</code> folder.</p>

    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="import io.github.ccxt.exchanges.Kraken;
import io.github.ccxt.exchanges.Bitfinex;
import io.github.ccxt.exchanges.Binance;
import io.github.ccxt.types.*;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

public class Example {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Create exchange instances
        Kraken kraken = new Kraken();
        Bitfinex bitfinex = new Bitfinex();

        Map<String, Object> config = new HashMap<>();
        config.put("apiKey", "YOUR_API_KEY");
        config.put("secret", "YOUR_SECRET");
        Binance binance = new Binance(config);

        // Load markets
        kraken.loadMarkets(false);
        binance.loadMarkets(false);

        // Public API
        OrderBook orderBook = kraken.fetchOrderBook("BTC/USDT");
        Ticker ticker = bitfinex.fetchTicker("BTC/USD");
        System.out.println(ticker.symbol + " last=" + ticker.last);

        // Fetch OHLCV
        var candles = binance.fetchOHLCV("BTC/USDT", "1h", null, 10L, null);
        System.out.println("Got " + candles.size() + " candles");

        // Private API (requires API keys)
        Balances balance = binance.fetchBalance();
        System.out.println("BTC free: " + balance.free.get("BTC"));

        // Place a limit buy order
        Order order = binance.createLimitBuyOrder("BTC/USDT", 0.001, 50000.0);
        System.out.println("Order id: " + order.id + " status: " + order.status);

        // Cancel it
        binance.cancelOrder(order.id, "BTC/USDT", null);
    }

<p dir="auto">All methods are also available as async variants returning <code>CompletableFuture</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-java notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">java</span>.<span class="pl-s1">util</span>.<span class="pl-s1">concurrent</span>.<span class="pl-s1">CompletableFuture</span>;

<span class="pl-c">// Fire multiple requests concurrently</span>
<span class="pl-smi">CompletableFuture</span><<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span>> <span class="pl-s1">btc</span> = <span class="pl-s1">binance</span>.<span class="pl-en">fetchTickerAsync</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">null</span>);
<span class="pl-smi">CompletableFuture</span><<span class="pl-smi">Ticker</span>> <span class="pl-s1">eth</span> = <span class="pl-s1">binance</span>.<span class="pl-en">fetchTickerAsync</span>(<span class="pl-s">"ETH/USDT"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">null</span>);
<span class="pl-smi">CompletableFuture</span>.<span class="pl-en">allOf</span>(<span class="pl-s1">btc</span>, <span class="pl-s1">eth</span>).<span class="pl-en">join</span>();
<span class="pl-smi">System</span>.<span class="pl-s1">out</span>.<span class="pl-en">println</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC: "</span> + <span class="pl-s1">btc</span>.<span class="pl-en">get</span>().<span class="pl-s1">last</span> + <span class="pl-s">" ETH: "</span> + <span class="pl-s1">eth</span>.<span class="pl-en">get</span>().<span class="pl-s1">last</span>);</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h4 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Error handling</h4><a id="user-content-error-handling" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Error handling" href="#error-handling"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Typed sync methods throw the underlying ccxt error directly — no <code>CompletionException</code>
unwrap needed. Catch exceptions in standard JDK order (most-specific first), like you
would with any other Java library:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-java notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">io</span>.<span class="pl-s1">github</span>.<span class="pl-s1">ccxt</span>.<span class="pl-s1">errors</span>.*;
<span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">io</span>.<span class="pl-s1">github</span>.<span class="pl-s1">ccxt</span>.<span class="pl-s1">exchanges</span>.<span class="pl-s1">Binance</span>;
<span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">io</span>.<span class="pl-s1">github</span>.<span class="pl-s1">ccxt</span>.<span class="pl-s1">types</span>.<span class="pl-s1">Order</span>;

<span class="pl-smi">Binance</span> <span class="pl-s1">binance</span> = <span class="pl-k">new</span> <span class="pl-smi">Binance</span>(<span class="pl-smi">Map</span>.<span class="pl-en">of</span>(<span class="pl-s">"apiKey"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"..."</span>, <span class="pl-s">"secret"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"..."</span>));
<span class="pl-k">try</span> {
    <span class="pl-smi">Order</span> <span class="pl-s1">order</span> = <span class="pl-s1">binance</span>.<span class="pl-en">createOrder</span>(<span class="pl-s">"BTC/USDT"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"limit"</span>, <span class="pl-s">"buy"</span>, <span class="pl-c1">0.001</span>, <span class="pl-c1">50000.0</span>);
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">InsufficientFunds</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {
    <span class="pl-c">// user error — show balance, don't retry</span>
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">InvalidOrder</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {                        <span class="pl-c">// covers OrderNotFound, DuplicateOrderId, …</span>
    <span class="pl-c">// user error — fix params</span>
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">AuthenticationError</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {                 <span class="pl-c">// covers PermissionDenied, AccountSuspended</span>
    <span class="pl-c">// refresh credentials</span>
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">RateLimitExceeded</span> | <span class="pl-smi">DDoSProtection</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {  <span class="pl-c">// multi-catch (Java 7+)</span>
    <span class="pl-smi">Thread</span>.<span class="pl-en">sleep</span>(<span class="pl-c1">30_000</span>);
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">NetworkError</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {                        <span class="pl-c">// RequestTimeout, ExchangeNotAvailable, …</span>
    <span class="pl-smi">Thread</span>.<span class="pl-en">sleep</span>(<span class="pl-c1">2_000</span>);                          <span class="pl-c">// transient — retry</span>
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">ExchangeError</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {                       <span class="pl-c">// any other exchange-side error</span>
    <span class="pl-c">// exchange refused</span>
} <span class="pl-k">catch</span> (<span class="pl-smi">BaseError</span> <span class="pl-s1">e</span>) {                           <span class="pl-c">// ccxt catch-all</span>
    <span class="pl-c">// unknown ccxt error</span>
}</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">
